summary: O3 RefApp Criteria-Based Reference Range Alerts
description:
Background & Rationale: 
Reference ranges are critical for interpreting clinical measurements such as vitals (e.g., blood pressure, temperature) and lab results (e.g., hemoglobin, creatinine). Currently, OpenMRS supports static reference ranges that do not account for patient-specific factors. However, in real-world clinical settings, normal values vary based on individual characteristics such as:
Age: Pediatric, adult, and elderly patients have different normal ranges.

Sex: Certain lab values differ between males and females (e.g., hemoglobin).

Pregnancy Status: Pregnancy alters normal physiological ranges.

Ethnicity: Some populations have distinct baseline values for specific lab tests.

Renal Function: Kidney disease stages impact reference ranges for labs like creatinine.

Weight/BMI: Obesity or underweight status influences some lab interpretations.

Time of Day: Circadian rhythms affect certain lab values (e.g., cortisol levels).

Objectives & Scope: 
This epic aims to implement factor-based reference ranges by modifying core OpenMRS components, including the data model, backend services (REST and FHIR2 modules), and frontend UI. The key goals include:
Extend Reference Range Model for Patient-Specific Factors → Modify the Concept Reference Range data structure to allow defining ranges based on patient factors.

Apply the Strictest Range When Multiple Factors Apply → Develop logic to evaluate overlapping criteria (e.g., age + pregnancy + renal function) and apply the most restrictive range.
Prioritize critical conditions over general rules (e.g., pregnancy overrides age-based ranges).


Update REST API to Support Factor-Based Ranges → Extend APIs to fetch the correct reference range based on patient details.

Enhance FHIR2 Module to Include Factor-Based Reference Ranges → Modify FHIR Observation resources to include factor-based ranges.

Implement UI for Managing Reference Ranges → A clinician should be able to set a different blood pressure range for children vs. adults in the UI.

Apply Factor-Based Reference Ranges in Observation Entry & Display → When entering vitals/lab results, the system should dynamically fetch and apply the correct reference range.
If a nurse enters blood pressure for a child, the system should flag 120/80 mmHg as high, while the same value is normal for an adult.
